truthBoundary: This gate pack defines what a GitHub user may safely trust today. It does not prove SEIS AGI, train or download a 512B model, run inference, run benchmarks, approve release, mutate GitHub, call providers, provision cloud/GPU resources, execute SSH, or grant route eligibility.

researchBaseline.seisImplication: GitHub readiness must include explicit governance, risk, transparency, measurement, and accountability boundaries before public AI capability claims.
Generative-AI public readiness must treat misuse, data, privacy, transparency, cybersecurity, and measurement risks as release gates, not marketing copy.
Long-horizon autonomy claims require task-duration and completion evidence; local demo behavior and green CI are not enough.
Abstract generalization claims require dedicated evaluation evidence; parameter count or installed assistants cannot prove AGI.

githubUserModes.label: Local Demo review
githubUserModes.allowedClaim: Users can inspect repository-local SEIS AI contracts, MCP resources, and validators.
githubUserModes.forbiddenClaim: Users cannot treat the repository as a trained 512B model or real AGI.

githubUserModes.label: Validator review
githubUserModes.allowedClaim: Users can run read-only validators that preserve the Local Demo and no-AGI boundary.
githubUserModes.forbiddenClaim: Passing validators cannot prove AGI, 512B training, 512B inference, or benchmark success.

githubUserModes.label: Real AGI use
githubUserModes.allowedClaim: No real AGI use is available today.
githubUserModes.forbiddenClaim: SEIS is not a routeable AGI or 512B inference system.

githubUserModes.label: Live provider use
githubUserModes.allowedClaim: Optional provider integrations may be configured later behind backend-only secrets.
githubUserModes.forbiddenClaim: No provider key is required or present for the core GitHub demo.
